description: FIX 1 (real bug): autostart's --restart always is silently lost when `up` recreates containers after `down`. Plumb a restart policy through podmanConfig and the three long-lived container run-argv builders, add an opt-in `-restart-always` flag to `up`, and auto-reapply the policy when a persisted marker (written by `autostart install`) or the LaunchAgent plist is present. Scope stays the three stack containers (wp-mysql, wp-wordpress, grimoire); ms365-login remains out of scope. Independent of FEAT-002; both touch podman.go so run sequentially.
steps: In cmd/grimoire-cli/podman_config.go, add a `RestartPolicy string` field to podmanConfig (document: empty = omit --restart, the current/default behavior; 'always' = set --restart=always on the three stack containers at create time). Leave defaultPodmanConfig() setting it to "" (no new flag in addFlags; the flag lives on `up` only). Do NOT add it to applyEnv.

In cmd/grimoire-cli/podman_argv.go, when c.RestartPolicy != "", insert `--restart=<policy>` (use the `--restart=always` single-token form) into the run argv of dbRunArgv(), webRunArgv(), and grimoireRunArgv() (place it among the `run -d --pod ... --name ...` flags, before the image). Do NOT add it to cliOneShotArgv() (the migrate one-shots are --rm throwaways) or to any pod-create argv.

In cmd/grimoire-cli/podman.go runPodmanUp, register a `-restart-always` bool flag (fs.Bool) with help text explaining it sets `--restart always` on the stack containers so autostart survives a down/up recreate. Resolve home via os.UserHomeDir() (tolerate error: skip detection if it fails). After parsing: if the flag is set, cfg.RestartPolicy = "always". Else if autostart is detected (marker file present, or fallback the LaunchAgent plist at launchAgentPath(home) exists), set cfg.RestartPolicy = "always" and print one line to w noting it is reapplying the autostart restart policy because autostart is configured (so the Fix-1 bug cannot silently recur). Update runPodmanUp's usage text to mention -restart-always and the auto-reapply behavior.

In cmd/grimoire-cli/podman_autostart.go, add `autostartMarkerPath(home string) string` returning e.g. filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share", "grimoire", "podman-autostart"). In podmanAutostartInstall, after wiring Layer A/B, os.MkdirAll the marker's dir (0o755) and os.WriteFile the marker (0o644, small content e.g. the machine name or a timestamp) and print that it was written. In podmanAutostartUninstall, os.Remove the marker (ignore os.IsNotExist) and report it. Keep the restartContainers() scope (three containers) unchanged.

Keep podmanUp pure/testable: the restart policy is carried on the cfg passed into podmanUp (which flows to the argv builders via ensurePodWithContainer's runArgv). Do NOT call os.UserHomeDir inside podmanUp or the argv layer; detection stays in the thin runPodmanUp layer in podman.go.
acceptance_criteria: With cfg.RestartPolicy="always", dbRunArgv/webRunArgv/grimoireRunArgv each contain `--restart=always`; cliOneShotArgv and the pod-create argv do NOT.
With cfg.RestartPolicy="" (default) none of the run argv contain `--restart` (unchanged behavior).

Driving podmanUp with fakeRunner and a cfg whose RestartPolicy="always" records a `run` for each of wp-mysql/wp-wordpress/grimoire that includes `--restart=always`; a plain run with RestartPolicy="" records none.
autostart install writes the marker file under a temp home; autostart uninstall removes it (asserted with t.TempDir()).
ms365-login never appears in any restart argv (existing TestUpdateRestartArgvInstallUninstall still green).
findings:
Implemented. Verification GREEN: `go build ./...`, `go test ./cmd/grimoire-cli/`, and `gofmt -l cmd/grimoire-cli` (no output) all pass.

Key facts for later steps (docs reconciliation etc.):
- Marker path (used by both `autostart install/uninstall` and `up` auto-detect): $HOME/.local/share/grimoire/podman-autostart, via new helper autostartMarkerPath(home string) string in cmd/grimoire-cli/podman_autostart.go. Dir created 0o755; file written 0o644 with content 'podman autostart installed <RFC3339 UTC timestamp>\n'. uninstall os.Remove's it, ignoring os.IsNotExist.
- Restart token form at container-create time is the SINGLE-TOKEN `--restart=always` (NOT the two-token `--restart always`). Added via new helper (c podmanConfig) restartFlag() []string in podman_argv.go, appended among the run flags (after `run -d --pod .. --name ..`, before the image) in dbRunArgv/webRunArgv/grimoireRunArgv ONLY. cliOneShotArgv and all pod-create argv are unchanged (no --restart).
- NOTE the distinction: autostart Layer A still uses the existing updateRestartArgv which builds the TWO-TOKEN `podman update --restart always <ctrs>` form (unchanged). The new single-token form is only on `podman run` at create time.
- New field: podmanConfig.RestartPolicy string (podman_config.go). Empty = omit --restart (default/historical behavior). NOT added to addFlags or applyEnv. defaultPodmanConfig() leaves it "".
- `up` flag: -restart-always (fs.Bool) in runPodmanUp (podman.go). When set => cfg.RestartPolicy="always". Else auto-reapply: os.UserHomeDir() (tolerates error) + autostartConfigured(home) which checks the marker first, then falls back to launchAgentPath(home); when detected sets cfg.RestartPolicy="always" and prints a one-line reapply notice to w. Detection lives in the thin podman.go dispatch layer; podmanUp and the argv builders never touch the filesystem/home.
- Scope unchanged: restartContainers() is still exactly [wp-mysql, wp-wordpress, grimoire]; ms365-login never appears in any restart argv.
- New tests (all passing): podman_argv_test.go TestRestartPolicyArgv + TestRestartPolicyEmptyOmitsFlag; podman_up_test.go TestUpRestartPolicyFlowsToRunArgv (fakeRunner, no live podman); podman_autostart_test.go TestAutostartMarkerInstallUninstall + TestAutostartConfiguredDetection (t.TempDir, fakeRunner). No test requires a live podman/DB/network.
